model_check.atmosphere: NRLMSIS 2.1, the U.S. Naval Research Laboratory’s empirical model of the air’s density at each height and place, given that day’s solar radio flux (10.7 cm: 174.1 solar flux units the day before, 149.3 averaged over 81 days) and geomagnetic activity (ap 4 at the time). The U.S. Standard Atmosphere 1976 takes its place when a day has none of these. NRLMSIS 2.1 was chosen over NRLMSISE-00 because it came nearer to the air measured between 30 and 70 km up, where a capsule slows: its density was off by 0.6 % from the TIMED/SABER satellite’s profiles of that day and 1.6 % from the Table Mountain laser radar’s (lidar’s) nights either side of it, against 3.7 % and 5.0 % for NRLMSISE-00. This is not a fully separate check: the rule for choosing was written after the landing results were known, and NRLMSIS 2.x was fitted to SABER’s measurements from 2002 to 2016.

model_check.note: From OSIRIS-REx’s reconstructed entry state, the entry model lands its capsule 6.6 km from where the recovery team found it (3.9 to 9.3 km over the published drag range; the limit is 10 km, met). It flies through NRLMSIS 2.1 for that day. With other air the distance is U.S. Standard Atmosphere 1976, 9.5 km (6.7 to 12.2); NRLMSISE-00, 12.1 km (9.4 to 14.8). The mission’s own simulation from the same state was 8.9 km off with its pre-flight atmosphere and 3.5 km with the day’s reconstructed one. Its 99 % landing area, 51.1 by 21.5 km, holds the real landing point.
